column1: # *** THE 1921 CENSUS - read 14 September 2026, the day before the trial expired. ***
# Findmypast holds it exclusively; it is not on FamilySearch at any price, and the 1931 returns were
# destroyed by fire, so this is the LAST census of the Taylor generation. Census date 19 JUNE 1921.
household
*** HENRY DALLING ***, 40, b.1881 Northam - *** INSURANCE AGENT, PEARL ASSURANCE COMPANY ***
column2: *** FORE STREET, NORTHAM *** - RG15 piece 10862, RD 286, sub-district 2, ED 5, schedule 50
column3: ISABEL TEMPLE DALLING, wife, 45; *** KATHLEEN GEORGINA, sister-in-law, 50 *** ; RONALD WILLIAM, son, 18, *** MOTOR MECHANIC *** for Mr George Boyle, Motor & Cycle Agents; SYLVIA MAY, daughter, 10; *** EDITH MAY, daughter, 8 *** (b.1913, new to this archive)
column4: *** THE ANSWER ON KATHLEEN, AND IT IS NOT A DATE - IT IS A LIFE. *** See below. Also: Henry Dalling was a GARDENER in 1911 and is an INSURANCE AGENT in 1921 - a change of class in ten years. And HORACE HENRY CHARLES, the eldest boy of 1911, is GONE from the house at twenty.

column1: *** HENRY ALBERT BURTON ***, 45, b.1876 Bermondsey - *** ASSURANCE AGENT, PRUDENTIAL ASSURANCE CO LTD, Holborn Bars, London ***
column2: *** 5 KINGSLEY TERRACE, BIDEFORD *** - RG15 piece 10855, RD 286, sub-district 1
column3: IRENE BURTON, wife, 42; CHARLES WILLIAM, son, 13, b. Bideford; and two BOARDERS - Boris F Matheson, 28, motor engineer, and Daisy M Matheson, 32
column4: *** TWO BROTHERS-IN-LAW IN THE SAME TRADE: *** Dalling for the Pearl, Burton for the Prudential. *** And ALBERT EDWARD BURTON, in the house in 1911, is NOT HERE. *** Only Charles William remains.

column1: *** ALFRED SIDNEY WOOD ***, 39, b.1882 South Pool, Devon - *** PAINTER, for C Wace House Decorator ***
column2: *** CHURSTON FERRERS *** (Brixham sub-district, Totnes RD) - RG15 piece 10510
column3: AGNES WALKER WOOD, wife, 31, b. Northam; *** SIDNEY WILLIAM HENRY, son, 1, b.1920 *** - a nephew new to this archive
column4: *** THE SOUTH DEVON CLUSTER IS CONFIRMED. *** Lucy's banns were called at CHURSTON FERRERS in 1909 and her brother William John was at PAIGNTON, three miles off, by 1911. In 1921 AGNES is living at Churston Ferrers. Three of the ten, eighty miles from where they were born.

column1: *** WILLIAM NORRISH SWEET ***, 35, b.1885 Tiverton - *** SHIPWRIGHT, H M DOCKYARD DEVONPORT ***
column2: *** 23 HAMILTON STREET, DEVONPORT *** (Keyham ward) - RG15 piece 10709
column3: LUCY ELIZABETH SWEET, wife, 39; *** KATHLEEN ALICE, daughter, 11, b.1910 ***
column4: *** THE NAMING DISCIPLINE AGAIN, and it is touching this time: *** Lucy called her daughter KATHLEEN - for the eldest sister who never married and was an invalid in another sister's house. *** And Lucy's birthplace is transcribed "NORTHAM, NORTHAMPTONSHIRE" *** - the second birthplace error in this one census.

column1: # ---- NOT FOUND IN 1921, and recorded as not found ----
# *** MARGARET HELEN WALKER BELL *** - 84 Margaret Helen/Ellen Bells of the right age in England and NOT
#   ONE born at Northam or in Devon. She had left the county and "Bell" is too common to follow blind.
# *** HORACE ARCHIBALD TAYLOR *** - two Horace Taylors in Devon, neither his. One, "WELSER H TAYLOR",
#   b.1875 at APPLEDORE in Northam parish, looked like a garbled Horace and was OPENED: he is a seaman
#   with a wife Belle and four children, and he is not ours. *** Checked rather than assumed. ***
# *** WILLIAM JOHN TAYLOR *** - not yet searched in 1921.
# *** MARY SEPTIMA *** - at the Cape by 1921 and so not in this census at all.
# ================ *** KATHLEEN GEORGINA TAYLOR: THE ANSWER *** ================
# This archive asked whether the eldest of the ten ever married. The 1911 census found her SINGLE at
# forty-one in her sister's house. The 1921 census finds her *** STILL THERE AT FIFTY *** - and gives
# the reason, in the occupation column:
#                        *** "HOME INVALID" ***
# *** That is not a date or a surname. It is a life. *** The eldest daughter of ten, unmarried at fifty,
# an invalid in her younger sister's house on Fore Street, with her brother-in-law the insurance agent
# and three children about her. She died in 1940, aged sixty-nine. Nothing in this archive had suggested
# it, because a tree records marriages and not infirmity.
# *** AND THE INDEX CALLS HER "KATHLEEN GEORGINA DALLING". *** She is a TAYLOR. The enumerator wrote the
# household's surname against every line and the transcriber followed him. *** THIS IS THE EXACT TRAP
# THAT COST THIS ARCHIVE A RETRACTION IN ARGENTINA *** - the 1895 Buenos Aires census, where "Lerena de
# L. Josefa" was read as a woman who married a Lerena and turned out to be household shorthand. The same
# enumerator's habit, in Devon, twenty-six years later, in English.
# ================ *** A BIRTHPLACE THAT IS SIMPLY WRONG, AND WHY *** ================
# The 1921 return gives IRENE's birthplace as *** BERMONDSEY, LONDON ***. She was born at NORTHAM in
# 1879 - her own marriage act of 30 August 1900 says so, and the 1911 census says so. Her husband HENRY
# ALBERT BURTON was genuinely born at Bermondsey. *** He filled the form - the transcript names "person
# making return" - and carried his own answer across to his wife's line. ***
# Recorded because it is a worked example of something this archive keeps meeting: *** a census
# birthplace is only as good as the person who filled the form, *** and one household member's answer
# can contaminate another's. Had Irene been met first in 1921, she would have been ruled out as a
# Londoner.
